row.title: j0k3r-pi project profile
row.content:
project: j0k3r-pi

purpose: personal/global pi agent configuration under ~/.pi/agent. it contains the primary orchestrator guide, workflow skills, markdown subagents, and local development copies of pi extensions used by the coding agent.

stack: typescript esm pi extensions, node 24+ runtime, vitest, typescript, typebox. context7 extension also uses @upstash/context7-sdk and @earendil-works/pi-ai. memory extension requires node:sqlite support.

important directories:
- agents.md: primary orchestrator rules for workflow gates, investigation, tdd, git, memory, and safety.
- skills/: global/user routing skills with registry contracts; load selected skill.md files from registry paths before relying on details.
- subagents/: markdown subagents; discovery is read-only and sdd-* agents execute formal sdd phases.
- extensions/: agent-dir extension implementations and readmes; project-local equivalents are .pi/extensions/<name>.
- docs/: supporting docs such as keyboard-shortcuts.md.
- .pi/memory.json: canonical memory project identity j0k3r-pi with project-scoped backups configured.
- subagents.json: global subagent model profiles and tool defaults.

core conventions:
- answer simple questions directly; treat investigation/review/diagnosis as read-only until the user approves a concrete implementation path.
- choose the lightest safe workflow: inline, simple tdd, discovery, or formal sdd/openspec.
- policy-sensitive files include agents.md, skills, subagents, permissions, memory/context config, and workflow/memory/permission/subagent/skill-registry extension code.
- strict tdd is required for non-trivial code changes.
- never commit, branch, tag, rebase, or push unless explicitly requested in the current conversation.
- use memory as a curated persistent brain; save durable non-sensitive decisions, commands, progress, todos, risks, and learnings.

sdd summary: formal sdd uses preflight git status, skill registry generation/reading, execution mode selection (interactive/normal/defaults), change slug/artifact store selection, and separate implementation approval. default named feature artifact store is hybrid. planning sequence is sdd-explore -> sdd-proposal -> sdd-spec -> sdd-design -> sdd-task; apply/verify/archive require their own approvals/state.

documented validation: from each extension directory, run npm test and npm run typecheck. examples: cd extensions/memory && npm test && npm run typecheck; cd extensions/subagents && npm test && npm run typecheck. these commands are documented but not yet verified in this memory seeding session.

risks/notes: permission guard config currently has bypassall true in both .pi/permissions.json and permissions.json, so enforcement validation can be masked until bypassall is false. do not store secrets in configs, skills, readmes, memories, or backups. context7 api key must be provided through the pi process environment only.

row.title: core orchestrator workflow gates
row.summary: j0k3r-pi uses a conservative orchestrator workflow: direct answers for simple questions, read-only investigation by default, lightest safe workflow selection, strict tdd for code, and explicit git commit/push approval.
row.content:
type: workflow rule
context: observed in agents.md and readme.md while seeding j0k3r-pi project memory.
rule: the main assistant is the orchestrator and keeps the user in control. answer simple questions directly without tools unless investigation is requested. treat investigation, review, diagnosis, analysis, comparison, and 'look at' requests as read-only; report evidence/options and wait for the user to approve a concrete implementation path. choose the lightest safe workflow: inline, simple tdd, discovery, or formal sdd/openspec. use strict tdd for non-trivial code changes. never commit, tag, branch, rebase, or push unless the user explicitly requests that git operation in the current conversation. before user-requested commits, save a substantive precommit progress memory checkpoint when there are meaningful changes.
implication: future agents should not treat diagnosis or passing tests as implementation or commit approval, and should ask concise clarifying questions when scope, success criteria, or approvals are unclear.

row.title: policy-sensitive change routing
row.summary: agent behavior changes are higher risk; use workflow-triage when impact is unclear, inline/docs-only only for small explicit localized wording/config fixes, and formal sdd when cross-cutting or durable behavior risk warrants artifacts.
row.content:
type: workflow rule
context: observed in agents.md plus skills/workflow-triage/skill.md and skills/sdd-workflow/skill.md.
policy-sensitive surfaces: agents.md; skills and subagents under .pi, .agents, ~/.pi/agent, or ~/.agents; .pi/permissions.json; .pi/memory.json; .pi/context7.json; .pi/subagents.json and ~/.pi/agent/subagents.json; workflow, memory, permission, skill-registry, or subagent extension code.
routing: if the user asks to investigate policy-sensitive behavior, stay read-only and report options first. before editing policy-sensitive files, state the selected workflow and why it is safe. use workflow-triage when scope/impact/routing is unclear. inline/docs-only is acceptable for small explicit localized low-risk edits. use formal sdd by default for multi-file, cross-cutting, future-agent-behavior, api/contract, or handoff-artifact work.
implication: do not downshift risky policy changes to casual edits just because they look like markdown/config, but also do not escalate small clear local wording fixes to full sdd unnecessarily.

row.title: formal sdd workflow protocol
row.summary: formal sdd requires git/skill-registry/mode preflight, prefers hybrid artifacts for named features, separates planning from implementation approval, and runs phase agents sequentially.
row.content:
type: workflow rule
context: observed in skills/sdd-workflow/skill.md and subagents/sdd-*.md.
protocol: before creating prd/openspec artifacts or launching sdd subagents, run git status --short, resolve dirty-worktree overlap, generate/read the skill registry, load relevant skill.md files from registry paths, resolve execution mode (interactive, normal, or defaults), choose a change slug/artifact store, and keep implementation approval separate from planning approval. default artifact store for named sdd features is hybrid: openspec files are source of truth and memory stores compact state/handoff.
sequence: new planning normally runs sdd-explore -> sdd-proposal -> sdd-spec -> sdd-design -> sdd-task, then stops before implementation unless apply is explicitly approved. sdd-apply implements approved task slices with strict tdd. sdd-verify reports issues without fixing. sdd-archive closes verified changes and syncs source-of-truth specs when applicable.
artifacts: canonical change spec is openspec/changes/<change>/spec.md; verification report is openspec/changes/<change>/verify-report.md; other common files are exploration.md, proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, and apply-progress.md.
implication: future agents should use subagents as phase executors only, not as workflow decision makers, and should require standard return envelopes with status, summaries, artifacts, memory ids, risks, validations, and next recommendation.

row.title: j0k3r-pi repository layout and extension stack
row.summary: the project is a ~/.pi/agent configuration repo containing orchestrator policy, skills, markdown subagents, docs, and local development copies of pi extensions implemented as typescript esm packages.
row.content:
type: architecture note
context: observed in readme.md, extension readmes, and package.json files.
layout: agents.md is the primary operating guide. skills/ contains routing-aware global/user skill.md files. subagents/ contains markdown-defined discovery and sdd phase agents. extensions/ contains local agent-dir pi extensions with project-local equivalents under .pi/extensions/<name>. docs/ contains supporting documentation such as keyboard-shortcuts.md. subagents.json defines global subagent model profiles/tool defaults; .pi/memory.json defines canonical memory project j0k3r-pi.
stack: extension packages are typescript esm packages with vitest and tsc --noemit validation. shared dependency is typebox; context7 additionally uses @upstash/context7-sdk and @earendil-works/pi-ai. memory uses node:sqlite, so node 24+ support matters.
extensions: agent-todo provides a single active branch todo and widget; context7 provides safe bounded documentation tools; memory provides project-aware sqlite/fts persistent brain; permission-guard provides in-process policy/audit; sidebar provides hud status; skill-registry generates skill routing indexes; subagents runs markdown subagents with history, model profiles, tool allowlists, and permission handoff.
implication: after changing extension code, markdown subagents, skills, or relevant configs during interactive pi sessions, tell the user to /reload or restart pi when the relevant docs require it.

row.title: subagent roles and boundaries
row.summary: discovery is a bounded read-only research subagent; sdd-* subagents execute formal phase work only under orchestrator control, with no subagent delegation and narrow memory/artifact permissions.
row.content:
type: workflow rule
context: observed in extensions/subagents/readme.md, skills/subagents-configuration/skill.md, and subagents/*.md.
roles: discovery is standalone/pre-sdd read-only evidence gathering for code, docs, pi docs, third-party docs, and context7 references; it must not choose workflow, edit files, create openspec artifacts, or save durable memory unless explicitly delegated. sdd-explore/proposal/spec/design/task may create/update only sdd artifacts under openspec/ and active sdd flow memory. sdd-apply may modify source code only for assigned approved tasks. sdd-verify reports issues and does not fix by default. sdd-archive closes verified sdd work and may sync openspec specs.
boundaries: subagents must not delegate or call subagent_* tools. the main agent remains the orchestrator and owns approvals, workflow routing, durable non-sdd memories, profile updates, and final user communication. subagents should use compact return envelopes and report permission blocks instead of retrying/bypassing.
configuration: global subagents live under ~/.pi/agent/subagents/*.md; project subagents live under .pi/subagents/*.md and override globals by normalized name. subagents.json merges model profiles by agent name and default tool allowlists must not include subagent_* tools.
implication: future agents should delegate only focused phase/research tasks with clear allowed/forbidden actions and should keep user approvals on the main thread.

row.title: security and configuration constraints
row.summary: secrets must stay out of repo files and memory; context7 keys use environment variables; memory backups are project-scoped; permission guard is not a sandbox and current bypassall true masks enforcement.
row.content:
type: constraint
context: observed in readme.md, extensions/context7/readme.md, extensions/memory/readme.md, extensions/permission-guard/readme.md, and current config files.
constraints: never store secrets, tokens, passwords, private keys, cloud tokens, or raw logs in skills, readmes, memories, .pi/*.json, extension config, or audit examples. context7 live calls require context7_api_key in the pi process environment; .pi/context7.json must contain only non-secret cache/default settings. memory cloud token fields must use env var names, not raw values. memory exports/imports use project-scoped mirror backups, with prompt audit export only when intentionally enabled. permission guard is an in-process policy guard, not os-level sandboxing; strong isolation requires external sandbox/container/micro-vm.
observed risk: both .pi/permissions.json and permissions.json currently set bypassall=true. enforcement validation can be misleading until bypassall is false, even though other policy fields are conservative (outside workspace ask, secrets deny, workspacereadonly allow, audit enabled).
implication: future agents should warn about bypassall before relying on permission enforcement and should recommend /reload or restart after permission/context/memory config changes.

row.title: documented validation and reload practices
row.summary: each extension documents npm test and npm run typecheck as local validation; registry and runtime changes may require /reload or restart before active pi behavior changes.
row.content:
type: workflow note
context: observed in readme.md and extension readmes while seeding project memory. commands are documented, not verified by execution in this session.
validation: from an extension directory, run npm test and npm run typecheck. examples include cd extensions/memory; npm test; npm run typecheck and cd extensions/subagents; npm test; npm run typecheck. memory docs currently expect 2 test files and 59 tests passing plus typecheck for that extension.
reload: after changing extension code, markdown subagents, skills, .pi/memory.json, .pi/context7.json, .pi/permissions.json, subagents.json, or related global config during an interactive pi session, tell the user to /reload or restart pi before relying on the new behavior.
keyboard/ui notes: agent-todo uses ctrl+space for todo widget; sidebar uses /sidebar or ctrl+.; subagents uses /subagents or ctrl+,; ctrl+o expands/collapses tool/rendered output in relevant contexts. avoid reserved global shortcuts documented in docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md when adding extension shortcuts.
implication: future agents should not store these as verified command memories until they run successfully, but can use them as documented validation guidance.
